clinician.final_diagnosis: cutaneous melanocytic tumor with CRTC1::TRIM11 fusion
clinician.trajectory_summary: An 18-year-old female presented with a slow-growing, occasionally tender, dull red mass on her left leg, present for three years. Initial B-ultrasound revealed a hypoechoic nodule in the subcutaneous soft tissue of the proximal left leg. A biopsy was performed, and histopathological examination showed a well-circumscribed nodular mass in the dermis, composed of epithelioid cells with features including visible mitosis and a positive basal margin. Immunohistochemistry confirmed the melanocytic nature of the tumor, showing positivity for S-100, SOX10, MelanA, and focally for HMB45, with a proliferation index of approximately 10%. Subsequent next-generation sequencing (NGS) detected a CRTC1::TRIM11 fusion, which was further confirmed by CRTC1 FISH. Six months post-operation, there was no evidence of local recurrence or metastasis.

key_supporting_evidence.claim: Patient presented with a slow-growing, occasionally tender, dull red mass on the left leg for three years.

Initial B-ultrasound identified a hypoechoic nodule in the subcutaneous soft tissue of the proximal left leg, measuring 1.2 × 1 cm, with distinct boundaries, uneven internal echo, enhanced posterior echo, and no clear blood flow signal.

The basal margin was positive.

Immunohistochemistry results were positive for S-100, SOX10, MelanA, and focally positive for HMB45, with INI1 and H3K27Me3 showing retention of nuclear expression, and a proliferation index hotspot area of approximately 10%.

Six-month postoperative follow-up revealed no local recurrence or metastasis.
